_comment: THE MAP. A route is a polyline whose vertices are lattice cells, every edge is a
straight road, and every direction change is an angle at a vertex (ADR 0095).
Read docs/HIGHWAY_LATTICE_PLAN.md section 4 before editing; the gate checks every
bound in section 5 on every vertex here and names the one that fails.
A cell is [q, r] on the triangular lattice: q steps east by lattice_cell_metres,
r steps 30 degrees east of north by the same. A level is lattice_level_metres of
height, level 0 being the combat plane. 'junction' on a vertex means THE EDGE
LEAVING THAT VERTEX is that tile, and the edge must be exactly the tile's
footprint: diverge_right is 3 cells, merge_below is 6. Junction tiles are
generated for the (n, 0) direction family only, which includes (0, n).
Saving this file relays the map out under the ship, the way saving tuning.cfg
re-tunes it. Legs are unequal on purpose (ADR 0085).
Ramps are lane routes and land with step C of the plan; these are the mainlines.
The trunk road, west to east. A to B is 11.4 km and B to C is 21.5 km along
the road, both within a per cent of what the retiring leg lengths said.
The two 15.3 degree vertices at (20,0) and (28,3) are an (8,3) edge: the
closest thing on any lattice to the 15 degrees nobody can have, and the
first direction change on this map anyone will fly.
The crossing road, D through B to E, riding two levels above the trunk.
It runs along e2, which is 60 DEGREES off the trunk's east — a lattice
angle, where the 55 degrees this map used to cross at is not, and a better
interchange angle besides (ADR 0095, plan section 7).
